entities.title: zazzle investigate --adaptive
entities.summary: The adaptive mode of `zazzle investigate` (`--adaptive`, `--agents`, `--orchestrator`, `--orchestrator-effort`, `--prose`, `--json`) and its review (`--review-model`, `--review-effort`) and benchmark (`--benchmark-model`, `--benchmark-effort`): each part of a question runs on the cheapest agent and effort that will do it, and an unsettled part goes up the ladder with what it established.
entities.purpose: mod.rs separates its flags from investigate's, builds the ladder (agent.rs: `MODEL`, `local:`, `claude:` or `codex:` specs, each `@EFFORT` or at low then high; by default the installed local models from `ai-agent status --json`, smallest first), rates the question 0 to 5 without a model, reads the task into items with ids and constraints (items.rs) and, above 0 with two items or more not all about one discovered component, asks a planner one rung above the difficulty to assign item ids to at most four `PART agent | I1,I2 | symbols` lines, held to a grammar when local and checked before dispatch with one repair (a refused repair runs the task as one assignment) (a planner that fails, gives no parts, rates its understanding low or asks to escalate is replaced by the next rung once). The parts run at the same time, each on its rung and with its own read session (calls.rs `all`, one thread per part): a local rung through investigate's lookup loop (explore and work, with --context for what an earlier attempt established), a hosted rung as one read-only `claude -p` or `codex exec` call whose reply lines are parsed and whose citations are checked (work.rs). A part escalates on a failure, a request to escalate, a low rating, rejected citations only or nothing verified, at most three times, never past the top or the time limit, and never when it is blocked on the user. A benchmark gets a reviewer by default, the strongest agent the machine can run (claude:opus at high effort when claude is installed, else the strongest hosted rung, else the strongest local one; --no-review leaves it out). The reviewer, with a benchmark, gets the wall-clock seconds, calls, tokens and cost zazzle measured for both results and must compare them on each of quality, time and tokens; one it leaves out is reported as not compared. With --orchestrator (any agent spec, usually claude: or codex:) it alone plans, with no ladder planner after it, combines and writes the --prose summary; otherwise the planner combines and the cheapest rung summarizes. The combiner cites only lines the parts verified, else they are merged. One deadline set when the job is accepted bounds it all: the main run (with a hosted benchmark beside it), a local benchmark and the review each end by their share of the time left, no part, escalation or model call starts after the deadline (calls.rs refuses it), and every report ends with the usage per role, an `orchestration` JSON object listing every step with its agent and tokens in and out, the orchestrator's apart from the delegated agents', and each adaptive run appends a text-free record to the orchestration log (record.rs). Calls that reported no token counts stay unknown in the usage, never zero, and a sink appends each call's usage to the job's run as it ends.
boundaries: Read-only: hosted agents run with Read, Grep and Glob only (claude, dontAsk) or a read-only sandbox (codex); local rungs use investigate's read-only lookups.
Only citations are checked, never claims; the report says the claims are the models'.
Hosted agents run only when --agents, --review-model or --benchmark-model names them; nothing is downloaded.
Local calls share daemon's one worker, so local parts take turns on it while hosted parts run beside them; the dedicated threads keep minutes-long agent calls off daemon's CPU pool.
